summary: Station [[Inspirit, Flagship Vessel]] to 8+ charge counters by T4-5 so every other artifact gains hexproof and indestructible, then spend its two charge counters a turn on draw or mana. Once protected, the artifact pile becomes hasty tramplers via [[Depthshaker Titan]] or [[Cyberdrive Awakener]] into [[Repurposing Bay]]. This is the sleeved list with [[Emry, Lurker of the Loch]] in for [[Urza, Lord High Artificer]], who hot-swapped out to become the commander of the new Urza box; Emry is the deck's only way to cast an artifact from the graveyard, and her affinity makes her cheap on a wide board.

phases.goal: Two mana pieces, Inspirit down on T3.
Station to 8, feed a charge sink, build draw.
One protected finisher behind Inspirit's hexproof-and-indestructible shield.

metrics.note: This is a single 1-for-1 hot-swap; no other card or land count changed. verify-2026-10-02/urza/build-report.md §7 (hot swap decision); CLAUDE.md Session Log 2026-10-02 (Inspirit entry)

swaps.reason: Urza moved to become the commander of the new Urza box, built around his own mana engine (27 artifacts there; this list has 41). Emry has affinity for artifacts (cheap once the board is wide) and is this deck's only way to cast a sacrificed or countered artifact from the graveyard -- the Cyberdrive line's second animation turn (recasting the Cyberdrive the Bay sacrificed) depends on her.
swaps.quoteOut: Tap an untapped artifact you control: Add {U}.
swaps.quoteIn: {T}: Choose target artifact card in your graveyard. You may cast that card this turn. (You still pay its costs. Timing rules still apply.)

keepers.why: A 1/2 body with no combat role looks cuttable, but it is the deck's only way to cast an artifact from the graveyard (One Last Job returns only creature, Vehicle and Equipment cards): it rebuys a sacrificed Cyberdrive Awakener, a countered finisher, or an artifact discarded to Thirst for Knowledge.
Does nothing until 30 counters are on board; it is the deck's grind win condition once the combo turn is answered, and Deepglow Skate or Tekuthal gets there fast.
A 3/3 with no combat text, but "whenever you cast a historic spell, draw a card" fires on nearly every artifact, legendary or Saga the deck plays.
A 3/3 vanilla-looking body; it adds 3 charge counters when it stations and proliferates on every tap, which is what pushes Inspirit to 8 a turn early.

Looks like a narrow sacrifice outlet, but it must already be in play before the Cyberdrive turn (a creature that arrives that turn can't tap), so it has to be kept in play a turn ahead of the combo, not fetched reactively.
A 1-mana counter with a drawback (the caster gets a 2/2 flying Bird) that looks like a sideboard card, but it is the deck's cheapest answer to a board wipe before the alpha swing.

pilotRules: On the kill turn, pay with lands: a tapped rock becomes a tapped creature once animated and can't attack.
Cyberdrive Awakener animates rocks cast this turn, but those are creatures that arrived this turn (CR 302.6): tap them for mana while paying for Cyberdrive, before it resolves.
Cyberdrive knocks an Equipment that's also a creature off anything it equips (CR 301.5c); never cast it on the Improvised Arsenal turn.
Never target Inspirit below 8 counters with Depthshaker Titan -- every target is sacrificed at the next end step, and sacrifice gets past indestructible.
Never add Final Showdown's "all creatures lose all abilities" mode to a wipe: Inspirit's own grant is a static ability, and losing it kills our own artifact creatures.
Traxos, Scourge of Kroog enters tapped; follow it with a historic spell (Emry, Sol Ring, Lost Jitte) before stationing, so it untaps and still has power to give.
Bygone Colossus is exiled at the next end step (recasting from exile costs {9}); station with it the same turn you warp it in.
Ripples of Potential phases Inspirit out until your next untap step; cast it only on an opponent's turn.
